full_judgment:
3. Short facts are that the predecessors of present respondent Nos.17-34 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.81 of 1994 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj for partition of the suit property and declaration that the RS record is wrong in respect of the suit land contending inter-alia that the suit land belonged to ex-landlords Bouddanath Sharma and others, who took khas possession of the suit land from the CS tenant and as they defaulted in paying rent the Zaminder of the suit land by pattan settlement gave to Montazuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-7), Abdul Hamid (predecessor of plaintiffs) and Mohammad Bepari (predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10) on 28th Poush of 1362 BS through Amalnama supported by Dakhila. But, in the Amalnama the shares of Montazuddin were wrongly written as 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti, while that of Abdul Hamid were 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 kranti. The original Amalnama was lost, but photocopy of that was with the plaintiffs. In spite of wrong insertion of shares in the name of Montazuddin, the three settlers possessed the suit land in equal shares and accordingly SA Khatian No.117 was rightly prepared in their names. Abdul Hamid died leaving behind his wife Amina Khatun, who inherited 1/3 share left by Abdul Hamid and she gifted that share equivalent to 0.861/2 acre by two Heba-bil-Ewaz deeds to plaintiff No.1, Md Panchu Dhali and plaintiff No.2 Saifunnessa. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent and mutated their names. The suit land was partitioned by metes and bounds. During RS preparation of record the names of plaintiffs were primarily recorded in the RS khatian Nos.233 and 380, but finally the names of the plaintiffs were omitted. The names of the defendants were recorded in the said RS Khatian omitting the names of the plaintiffs. On the basis of these wrong RS records, the defendants are claiming additional land in which they have no right. So, the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land became clouded. The plaintiffs requested the defendants in the first part of Ashar of 1401 BS for partition, which was denied by the defendants. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 5. Defendant Nos.1-7 contended, inter-alia, that their predecessor Montazuddin took the suit land by pattan/ settlement of 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti and he also took settlement of remaining 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 karas and 2 krantis in the Benami of Abdul Hamid. Practically Montazuddin was owner of 16 annas, i.e. 2.59 acres of land. Montazuddin paid rent by himself in the Zaminder's Seresta for the entire suit land and had been in possession of the entire suit land by erecting dwelling house and by cultivation. Abdul Hamid never possessed the suit land nor did he pay rent thereof. In the year 1961 Abdul Hamid requested Montazuddin to accord permission for Mohammad Bepari to live in some portion of the suit land and, therefore, Montazuddin permitted Mohammad Bepari to live in a small part of the suit land. In SA khatian, owner Montazuddin, his Benamder Abdul Hamid and licensee Mohammad Bepari's names were recorded. Montazuddin paid rents for the suit land and died leaving defendant Nos.1-7, who had been in possession of the suit land. Before preparation of RS record 10 decimals from plot No.60 and 17 decimals from plot No.63 were occupied by the Government for constructing road and only 1.44 acres of land was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1-6 in RS khatian No.223. In order to avoid litigation, the defendants admitted this RS record. The plaintiffs' deeds are forged. Abdul Hamid possessed only 2 annas and he had two wives. So, the plaintiffs cannot claim more than the share inherited by each wife. Defendant Nos.1- 7 possessed 1.44 acres of land. The plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 have no possession. So, the suit should be dismissed. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 8-10 contended, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Zaminder Mohini Kumar Dey and Kangali Dey and they settled the suit land to Mohammad Bepari and put him in possession. At the time of SA record, SA khatian No.117 was correctly made in the name of Montazuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid and Mohammad Bepari. By amicable partition total 2.59 acres of land was possessed by them erecting dwelling houses in equal shares. Mohammad Bepari got 0.86 acre of land in his share. Mohammad Bepari's name was correctly recorded in the RS khatian No.580. Mohammad Bepari died leaving behind 3 sons (defendant Nos.8-10), one daughter Rana Akter and wife Morjina Begum, and the heirs have been possessing 0.82 acre of land by putting pillars and 0.04 acre in ejmali in the pond. The plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land. So, the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable. Defendant Nos. 8-10 prayed for a separate saham of 0.86 acre of land. 

 7. The trial court decreed the suit for partition on contest in preliminary form against the defendant Nos. 1-7 and 8-10 and ex-parte against the rest. RS khatian No. 223 was also declared wrong and not acted upon. Plaintiffs were given 86.5 decimal of land and defendant Nos. 8-10 were given 86 decimal of land by the preliminary decree. 

 8. Being aggrieved, defendant Nos.1-7 preferred Title Appeal No.83 of 1996 before the District Judge, Munshigonj challenging that the defendant Nos. 8-10 were not entitled to get any share and RS record No. 223 that was declared wrong is illegal. On transfer the appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, Munshigonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 8-10-1998 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Then defendant Nos.1-7 filed Civil Revision No.623 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was made absolute in part by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in Title Appeal No. 83 of 1996 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. The judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court in Title Suit No. 81 of 1994 so far as it relates to giving 1/3 share of saham to the defendant Nos. 8-10 declaring the RS Khatian No. 223 wrong was also set-aside. 

 16. Believing the said Amalnama the High Court Division finally held that the judgment and decree passed by the court of appeal below affirming the decision of the trial Court giving 1/3 saham to the defendant Nos.8-10 and the declaration that RS Khatian No.223 as wrong are not sustainable in law. 

 17. Plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that actually settlement was taken equally in the name of Montazuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid Sarder and Mohammad Bepari. In spite of wrong insertion of share in the settlement deed Montajuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid Sarder and Mohammad Bepari possessed the suit land in equal shares and during SA operation the SA Khatian No. 117 has rightly been prepared in the names of these three settlers as the owner of the schedule land. 

 18. The trial court judged that the title and possession of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 are proved by dint of the oral and documentary evidence adduced therein. It was also proved that the SA khatian No. 117 was correctly recorded in the names of the predecessors of the contesting parties in equal shares. Moreover, possession of defendant Nos. 8-10 and that of the plaintiffs are also admitted by the defendant nos. 1-7. The defendant nos. 1-7 or their predecessor neither protested the separation of jama nor the mutation in the names of the defendant Nos.8-10 regarding the 1/3 portion of the suit land. 

 20. On the basis of documentary evidences it is proved that the defendant Nos. 1-7 could not establish the settlement to be genuinely a deed of title. And it is evident that the same is a rent receipt having incorporated the essential ingredients of a rent receipt. Moreover, the said rent receipt does not include the name of the predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10. But, subsequently, during the operation of SA record of rights the defendant Nos. 8-10's predecessor got his name recorded in SA Khatian and strengthen his title in the suit land on par with the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7. The said SA Khatian not being challenged by the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7 had acted upon. 

 "On the second question it is urged by the learned Counsel for the appellants that the High Court Division has acted beyond its jurisdiction in reversing the concurrent findings of fact of the two courts below disregarding the norms of interference. It cannot be gainsaid that a finding of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court is binding on the High Court, as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of material evidence affecting the merit of the case. In this case it does not appear that there is any such error of law in the findings of the trial court and the lower appellate court. It is borne out from the judgment of the lower appellate court in particular that besides the oral evidence the sale deeds and the SA Khatian on the basis of which the rents were alleged to have been paid by the plaintiffs through rent receipts have been duly considered by the said court which is the final court of fact. We are therefore of the opinion that the learned Judges of the High Court Division were not correct in reversing the concurrent decisions of the courts below." 

 27. The positive findings of the courts below as mentioned above were wrongly interfered by the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The High Court Division totally misdirected itself in holding that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of the trial Court giving 1/3 saham to the defendant Nos.8-10 and declaration RS Khatian No.223 as wrong are not sustainable in law.
